title: The reranker that scored nothing
blurb: Failed batches got neutral scores instead of being marked unscored.
prompt: Retrieval quality dropped without an alarm, because failed rerank batches were assigned neutral scores and low-value passages climbed. The same response truncated long passages silently and never reported it. Review it, fix it, and prove unscored is not a score.
aiNote: The draft maps failed rerank batches to a neutral score, so infrastructure failures are indistinguishable from genuine mid-tier relevance and silently reorder results, and it truncates passages without a marker so scores describe text the model never saw.
testIdea: Fail one batch of 64 and assert those passages are marked unscored and keep their retrieval order; truncate a 6 KiB passage and assert the response reports truncation; bump the model version and assert old scores are not served.
followUps: When should reranking fail the whole request?
How would you validate reranking lift offline?
Why is a score histogram useful in production?
